summary.headline: Sell practical, human-supervised AI workflow improvements to UK SMEs before building a product.
summary.best_opportunity: Fixed-scope AI workflow implementation with optional monthly support.
summary.why_now: DSIT's 2025 survey of 3,500 UK businesses, published in 2026, found 16% using AI, with limited skills and unclear use cases among common blockers. Adopters often reported productivity and process gains, but most had not seen revenue change; sell measurable time savings rather than AI hype.

top_opportunities.name: SME AI workflow implementation and support
top_opportunities.description: Implement one small, human-reviewed admin workflow using a client's existing software, with handover and optional monthly monitoring.
top_opportunities.why_now: DSIT found adoption still modest at 16%, and readiness gaps among intending adopters. It is a skills/use-case opportunity, not evidence of guaranteed willingness to pay.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-managed UK firms with 5-50 staff, especially business services, administration and property teams.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potential first paid pilot in 1-3 weeks through direct sales; uncertain until validated.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £150-£500/month for monitoring, maintenance and incremental workflow improvements, subject to pilot results.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a software engineer: integration and safe delivery skills transfer directly.
risks: Prospects may not have budget or a sufficiently costly workflow; quantify the baseline first.
Data protection, access control and inaccurate model outputs require human oversight and clear scope.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best near-term bet: sell one measurable outcome as a service before investing in SaaS.

top_opportunities.name: Lead-response automation for local service businesses
top_opportunities.description: Connect incoming web enquiries to rapid acknowledgement, owner alerts, a simple pipeline and follow-up reminders, retaining human control of sales messages.
top_opportunities.why_now: Fast response and missed enquiries are measurable operational pain points; the demand hypothesis needs local customer interviews and paid pilots.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades, property services and appointment-based small businesses handling inbound leads manually.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150-£700 for automation services, test environment and outreach.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1-3 weeks if a business accepts a paid setup pilot.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £100-£400/month for monitoring, fixes and simple conversion reporting.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong match for integration and reliability skills.
risks: Third-party integration changes can create ongoing support work.
Personal-data handling and automated communications need careful compliance and testing.
top_opportunities.verdict: Promising narrow offer if a buyer confirms missed-lead costs and agrees to a pilot.

top_opportunities.name: Local-business website care and enquiry conversion
top_opportunities.description: Improve a small business website's enquiry path, forms, analytics and reliability, then offer hosting, updates and conversion maintenance.
top_opportunities.why_now: Simple to explain and deliver quickly, but the live evidence reviewed did not quantify current local demand; validate a specific niche rather than assume a gap.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades, clinics and independent professional firms with dated websites or poor enquiry flows.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100-£500 using existing engineering skills and low-cost hosting.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1-4 weeks; a deposit can precede build work.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £40-£200/month for hosting, updates, backups and reporting.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong technically; control scope and client content delays.
risks: Crowded market and price competition from templates and agencies.
Slow approvals can reduce effective hourly earnings.
top_opportunities.verdict: Reliable fallback service when differentiated by niche and enquiry outcomes.

top_opportunities.name: Niche operational micro-SaaS
top_opportunities.description: Find one repeated admin task in a tightly defined UK trade or professional niche, deliver it manually first, then build only after paid validation.
top_opportunities.why_now: Recurring software revenue is attractive, but this research did not uncover a specific underserved workflow or confirmed willingness to pay.
top_opportunities.buyer: A defined trade or small professional-services segment identified through interviews.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300-£1,500 for a basic prototype and hosting; avoid paid acquisition before validation.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Typically 4-12+ weeks; faster only with pre-sold design partners.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Subscription potential; pricing must be tested with buyers.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High technical fit; customer discovery and distribution are the main challenge.
risks: Building without paid validation risks wasting time and budget.
Existing tools may already solve the problem, and support costs can erode margins.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not build beyond a prototype until several target buyers commit to paid pilots.

top_opportunities.name: Local niche lead-generation service
top_opportunities.description: Create a focused landing page and qualification funnel for one high-value local category and sell opted-in enquiries under an explicit quality agreement.
top_opportunities.why_now: Cheap to test, but this run found no location-specific traffic, lead cost or buyer-conversion evidence; verify economics before scaling.
top_opportunities.buyer: One or two providers in a high-value local service category, such as specialist trades or property services.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200-£1,000 for landing page, tracking and capped traffic tests.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 2-8 weeks depending on traffic, conversion and a buyer agreement.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly fee or per-qualified-lead income if quality and volume persist.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit; requires sales and marketing iteration.
risks: Acquisition costs can exceed revenue; verify unit economics before spending further.
Consent, privacy and disputes about lead quality can undermine the model.
top_opportunities.verdict: Run a capped test only after a buyer defines a qualified lead and agrees terms.

best_pick.name: SME AI workflow implementation and support
best_pick.why_it_wins: It offers the quickest route to paid validation without committing the £2,000 budget to a speculative product. DSIT's representative 3,500-business survey found 16% AI adoption, common skills/use-case barriers, and self-reported productivity or process benefits among many adopters. This supports an implementation hypothesis, not a guarantee of demand; most adopters had not yet seen revenue change.
validation_plan: Choose one niche and interview 10 owners about repetitive admin; quantify time, errors and current workaround.
Offer three qualified prospects a fixed-scope paid pilot; proceed to monthly support only if at least one pays and the result is measurable.
best_pick.first_offer: £350 fixed-price workflow review and one supervised automation pilot, with baseline, staff handover and 30-day check-in; offer support separately after results.
best_pick.mvp: One workflow built on the client's existing tools, with least-privilege access, exception logging, testing and human approval for external or consequential outputs.
customer_types: Small recruitment, accountancy or business-services teams with repetitive document and inbox work
Owner-managed local service firms manually handling and chasing web enquiries
best_pick.do_today: Select one niche, write a one-page outcome-led offer, and contact 15 local decision-makers for short workflow interviews rather than generic AI demos.
